insight: Open PRs against main so a merge deploys to prod; a feature-branch base silently never ships. The pr-base-guard hook enforces this.
A test that never failed proves nothing (false-green). The red-quality-gate blocks GREEN until a test demonstrably fails for the right reason.

CI should run only checks you'd act on, at the cheapest trigger: PRs to main (not every push), concurrency-cancel, expensive jobs gated behind fast ones, timeouts. Tests nobody acts on waste Actions minutes. See .claude/templates/ci.yml.

A cheap CI gate that tests nothing is worse than a slow one: it reports green so nobody looks. One repo's only required check ran 5 spec files out of 1020 because it was pointed at tests/unit while the house rule co-locates tests with source. Measure gate COVERAGE (files the required check runs / files that exist) before measuring cost. See .claude/skills/ci-audit.

`paths-ignore` on a workflow trigger whose job is a REQUIRED status check blocks docs-only PRs forever — the check never reports, so the rule never satisfies. Always run the job; skip the expensive part in a step, and fail open when the changed-file lookup fails.

vitest's fileParallelism is global. Set to false for the suites sharing one Postgres, it serializes every pure test too — 27 minutes for a suite whose 80% DB-free half runs in 90 seconds parallel. Split into two configs and route per file by what the source reaches for, not by directory (co-location makes paths meaningless) or filename convention (only 29 of ~200 DB specs followed it).

The 'CI-gated e2e: skip don't throw' rule has a failure mode: if CI never SETS the flag, the suite is collected, skipped, green, and inert forever. One repo spent ~290s of setup per run to execute a single test because 16 of 24 spec files gated on a variable no workflow set. Set the flag in a scheduled job and read the skip count — '48 skipped' is absent, not passing.

A migration post-condition asserting a production row count (`if still_open <> 10 then raise`) fails on CI's fresh unseeded database, exits `supabase start` non-zero, and kills every job that needed a DB — before any test runs. It read as a test failure for weeks. Assert the rows the migration targeted, not the corpus; and prove the guard can still REJECT, or it is vacuous.

Repairing broken CI without also cutting its scope costs MORE, not less: a green expensive suite runs to completion where a broken one died at setup in four minutes. Estimated ~$104/mo -> ~$203/mo for the repair alone, vs ~$3/mo for repair plus the trigger and suite-split cuts. Do both in one change.

A copy-once starter only reaches NEW repos; every adopted repo drifts and nothing detects it. The audited repo's hand-edited CI was worse than the template it came from. Ship a pull-based auditor (/ci-audit) alongside the template, and run it once after adoption.
